en: to be ravenous; to be possessed by a gluttonous spirit

examples.en: Today I ate like a starving person.

examples.ko: 하루 종일 굶었더니 걸신들린 것 같아요.
examples.en: I haven't eaten all day, so I feel ravenous.

examples.ko: 동생이 걸신들렸는지 라면을 세 개나 먹어요.
examples.en: My brother must be starving, since he's eating three packs of ramen.

examples.ko: 걸신들려서 음식을 마구 먹다 보면 체해요.
examples.en: If you gobble food like a starving person, you get indigestion.
Why are you eating like you're starving?
I guess I'm so hungry that I'm devouring everything.

explain: 음식을 몹시 탐내며 허겁지겁 먹는 모습에 써요. 보통 '걸신들린 것처럼', '걸신들린 듯이'처럼 말하고, 놀리는 느낌이 있어서 어른께는 조심해요. 비슷하게 '게걸스럽게 먹다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I was hungry, so I ate like a starving person.
phrases.nuance_ko: '걸신들린 것처럼'과 같은 뜻이고, 먹는 모습을 말할 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same as '걸신들린 것처럼'; the most common form for describing the way someone eats.

phrases.example: 하루에 다섯 끼나 먹다니 걸신들렸나 봐요.
phrases.en: Eating five meals a day, I must have a bottomless stomach.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기나 친한 사람이 너무 많이 먹을 때 장난으로 하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A joking remark about oneself or a close friend eating too much.

phrases.en: The child is gobbling down the bread.
phrases.nuance_ko: '걸신들리다'와 비슷하게 탐욕스럽고 허겁지겁 먹는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '걸신들리다'; describes eating greedily and hastily.

explain_en: It describes someone eagerly wolfing down food. It usually appears as '걸신들린 것처럼' or '걸신들린 듯이', and it has a teasing tone, so be careful with elders. A similar expression is '게걸스럽게 먹다'.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 부모님과 경양식 식당에서 돈가스를 먹었어요.
examples.en: As a kid, I ate pork cutlet with my parents at a Western-style restaurant.

examples.ko: 이 골목에는 오래된 경양식 집이 아직 남아 있어요.
examples.en: An old Western-style restaurant still remains in this alley.

examples.ko: 할머니는 오늘 경양식을 먹으러 가자고 하셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother suggested we go eat Western-style food today.

examples.ko: 옛날 경양식 분위기가 그리워서 일부러 찾아갔어요.
examples.en: I missed the old-style Western restaurant atmosphere, so I went on purpose.

examples.ko: 경양식 돈가스에 밥과 샐러드가 같이 나왔어요.
examples.en: The Western-style pork cutlet came with rice and salad.
Shall we have Western-style food for lunch today?

explain: '돈가스, 함박스테이크' 같은 한국식 서양 요리를 말해요. 요즘은 그냥 '양식'이나 '레스토랑'이라고 더 자주 하고, '경양식'은 옛날 분위기의 식당을 떠올릴 때 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 경양식 돈가스에는 수프와 빵이 같이 나와요.
phrases.en: Old-style pork cutlet comes with soup and bread.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛날식으로 소스를 얹은 돈가스를 떠올리게 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Brings to mind the old-style cutlet with sauce on top.

phrases.example: 옛날 경양식 집에 가면 어릴 때가 생각나요.
phrases.en: Going to an old-fashioned western diner reminds me of childhood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 추억이나 옛날 분위기를 말할 때 '옛날'과 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired with '옛날' when talking about nostalgia.

phrases.en: Shall we have western food for dinner tonight?
phrases.nuance_ko: 요즘은 '경양식'보다 '양식'이라는 말을 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: These days '양식' is used more often than '경양식'.

explain_en: Old-fashioned Western restaurant food like cutlets; a type of cuisine only. It refers to Korean-style Western dishes such as '돈가스' and '함박스테이크'. Today people more often just say '양식' or '레스토랑', and '경양식' tends to evoke old-fashioned restaurants.

examples.en: My grandfather fished at sea when he was young.

examples.ko: 아버지는 배를 타고 고기잡이해서 우리를 키우셨어요.
examples.en: My father raised us by fishing from a boat.

examples.ko: 이 마을 사람들은 대부분 고기잡이하며 살아요.
examples.en: Most people in this village live by fishing.
I saw people fishing in the river on the weekend.

examples.ko: 날씨가 나빠서 오늘은 고기잡이하러 못 나가요.
examples.en: The weather is bad, so we can't go out fishing today.
The boat that had been fishing suddenly came back to port.

explain: '낚시하다'는 취미로 즐기는 느낌이고, '고기잡이하다'는 생계나 일로 그물이나 배를 써서 잡는 느낌이 있어요. 명사 '고기잡이'로 '고기잡이를 나가다', '고기잡이배'처럼도 많이 말해요. 같은 일을 딱딱하게 말하면 '어업'이에요.

phrases.en: My father goes out fishing at dawn.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고기잡이하다'보다 일하러 바다로 나가는 장면이 분명하게 그려져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Compared with 고기잡이하다, it paints a clearer picture of heading out to sea for work.

phrases.en: Many fishing boats are floating on the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고기를 잡는 일에 쓰는 배를 가리키는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common compound for the boat used for fishing work.

phrases.en: My father catches fish at sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 비슷하지만 더 쉽고 일상적인 말이라 일이든 취미든 두루 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning, but simpler and everyday; it works for both work and hobby.

explain_en: '낚시하다' feels like a hobby, while '고기잡이하다' suggests fishing as a livelihood or job, using nets and boats. The noun '고기잡이' is also common, as in '고기잡이를 나가다' and '고기잡이배'. The more formal word for the industry is '어업'.

examples.en: This tangerine has soft and sweet flesh.
I blended grape pulp to make juice.

examples.ko: 과육 속에 작은 씨가 박혀 있어요.
examples.en: Small seeds are embedded in the flesh of the fruit.
The flesh is yellow and the skin is thin.
I like that you can chew pieces of pulp in this juice.

examples.ko: 오렌지는 껍질을 벗기고 과육만 골라 먹었어요.
examples.en: I peeled the orange and ate only the flesh.

explain: 음료 포장에 '과육 함유'라고 쓰이거나 요리와 과일을 설명할 때 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 보통 '과일'이라고 말해요.

phrases.example: 이 복숭아는 과육이 풍부해서 정말 맛있어요.
phrases.en: This peach has plenty of flesh, so it's really delicious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과일을 설명할 때 먹는 부분이 많고 부드럽다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe fruit that has plenty of soft edible flesh.

phrases.example: 바나나 과육을 으깨서 빵 반죽에 넣었어요.
phrases.en: I mashed the banana pulp and put it in the bread dough.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리할 때 과일의 속을 부수는 과정을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in cooking when you mash the inside of a fruit.

phrases.example: 이 주스에는 과육이 들어 있어서 씹는 맛이 있어요.
phrases.en: This juice contains pulp, so it has something to chew.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음료나 식품 포장에서 자주 보는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often seen on drink and food packaging.

explain_en: It often appears on drink packaging as '과육 함유' (contains fruit pulp) and when explaining cooking or fruit. In everyday conversation people usually just say '과일'.

en: ingredients for soup; meat and vegetables for soup

examples.ko: 국거리 고기를 한 근 사 왔어요.
examples.en: I bought a pound of meat for soup.
At the market I picked out ingredients for seaweed soup.

examples.ko: 냉장고에 국거리가 없어서 오늘은 찌개를 끓여요.
examples.en: There's nothing for soup in the fridge, so I'm making stew today.
Please cut the radish for the soup into big pieces.
What should we use for the soup today?
I bought beef brisket for the soup.

explain: 국이나 탕에 넣을 고기, 채소, 해물 같은 재료를 한꺼번에 가리켜요. 마트에서 '국거리용 고기'처럼 붙어 있는 것을 볼 수 있어요. '반찬거리'처럼 '-거리'가 붙으면 만들 음식의 재료라는 느낌이 돼요.

phrases.en: I bought beef to use for soup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 국에 넣기 좋게 잘라 파는 고기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to meat sold cut for putting into soup.

phrases.en: I prepared the ingredients for tonight's soup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 국을 끓이기 전에 재료를 챙기는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to getting ingredients ready before making soup.

phrases.en: I washed the soup vegetables thoroughly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고기뿐 아니라 국에 넣을 채소도 '국거리'라고 부를 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Not only meat, but vegetables for soup can also be called 국거리.

explain_en: Meat or vegetables bought for making soup (국, 찌개) It covers meat, vegetables, seafood and other ingredients that go into a soup. At supermarkets you can see labels like '국거리용 고기'. With '-거리', as in '반찬거리', it gives the feel of ingredients for a dish you will make.

examples.en: In winter I bought and ate chrysanthemum pastries on the street.
These chrysanthemum pastries have red bean paste in them.

examples.ko: 국화빵이 따뜻할 때 먹으면 더 맛있어요.
examples.en: The chrysanthemum pastry tastes better when it's warm.
Please give me one chrysanthemum pastry too.
Chrysanthemum pastries differ from fish-shaped pastries only in shape.

examples.ko: 학교 앞 국화빵 가게는 항상 줄이 길어요.
examples.en: The chrysanthemum pastry shop in front of the school always has a long line.

explain: 국화 모양 틀에 반죽을 붓고 속에 팥 같은 것을 넣어 구운 겨울 길거리 간식이에요. 비슷한 간식인 '붕어빵'은 물고기 모양이라서 모양으로 구분해요. 두 간식 모두 겨울에 길에서 팔아요.

phrases.en: A bag of chrysanthemum pastries is 2,000 won.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길거리에서 사 먹을 때 양을 말하는 흔한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common way to state the amount when buying from a street vendor.

phrases.example: 아저씨가 틀에 반죽을 부어 국화빵을 구워요.
phrases.en: The vendor pours batter into the mold and bakes chrysanthemum pastries.
phrases.nuance_ko: 만드는 사람이 하는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes what the person making them does.

phrases.example: 추운 날에는 따끈한 국화빵이 먹고 싶어요.
phrases.en: On cold days I want some warm chrysanthemum pastries.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겨울 간식의 따뜻한 느낌을 살려 주는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing that brings out the warm feel of this winter snack.

explain_en: It is a winter street snack baked in a chrysanthemum-shaped mold, with filling such as red bean paste. The similar '붕어빵' is fish-shaped, so you tell them apart by shape. Both are sold on the street in winter.

examples.en: I boiled cockles and dipped them in seasoned sauce.
Cockles are in season in winter, so they taste great.
I ordered cockle bibimbap and it was really delicious.
Cockles have ridges on their shells.
I bought a bag of cockles at the market.
Wash the cockles well and let them spit out sand first.

explain: 삶아서 양념에 무쳐 먹는 '꼬막무침'이나 '꼬막비빔밥'으로 많이 만나요. 그냥 '조개'라고 해도 되지만 꼬막은 메뉴 이름에서 따로 구별해서 불러요.

phrases.en: I ordered seasoned cockles at the restaurant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 삶은 꼬막을 양념에 무친 음식 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name of a dish of boiled cockles mixed with seasoning.

phrases.en: Cockle bibimbap is spicy and tasty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꼬막을 올려 비벼 먹는 밥 메뉴예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A rice dish topped with cockles that you mix together.

phrases.example: 꼬막을 삶을 때는 너무 오래 삶지 마세요.
phrases.en: When you boil cockles, don't boil them too long.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꼬막을 요리할 때 '삶다'와 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with '삶다' when cooking cockles.

explain_en: You mostly meet it as seasoned boiled cockles (꼬막무침) or cockle bibimbap. You could just say '조개', but on menus cockles are named separately.

examples.en: My mother made a refreshing nabak-kimchi.

examples.ko: 나박김치 국물이 시원해서 자꾸 먹게 돼요.
examples.en: The nabak-kimchi broth is so refreshing that I keep eating it.

examples.ko: 고기를 먹을 때 나박김치를 같이 먹어요.
examples.en: I eat nabak-kimchi together when I have meat.
Radish and cabbage go into nabak-kimchi.
The nabak-kimchi at this place is really delicious.
When the nabak-kimchi ripens, it gets even more refreshing.

explain: 국물이 많은 물김치라서 배추김치와 달리 국물을 같이 떠먹어요. 맵지 않고 시원한 맛이라 기름진 음식이나 떡과 잘 어울려요. 김치지만 반찬이면서 국처럼 먹는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I make nabak-kimchi on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 김치를 만들 때 쓰는 '담그다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it with 담그다, the verb for making kimchi.

phrases.en: I ate tteokbokki with cool nabak-kimchi.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맛과 온도를 말하는 '시원한'과 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired with 시원한 for its cool, fresh taste.

phrases.en: I drank a bowl of nabak-kimchi broth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 국물까지 먹는 김치라서 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase since the broth is eaten too.

explain_en: It is a watery kimchi, so unlike napa cabbage kimchi you also scoop up and drink the broth. It is mild and refreshing, so it goes well with oily food or rice cakes. It is a side dish but is eaten a bit like a soup.

examples.en: I boiled mung beans into porridge and ate it.
I bought a bag of mung beans at the market.
My mother made mung bean pancakes for me.
They say mung bean porridge is good for the body in hot summer.
You have to soak the mung beans and grind them.
Bean sprouts are sprouted from mung beans.

explain: 한국 음식에서는 '녹두전'(빈대떡), '녹두죽'처럼 요리 이름에 많이 붙어요. 숙주나물도 녹두로 키우는 거라 같이 알아 두면 좋아요. 껍질을 벗긴 녹두는 노란색이에요.

phrases.en: On rainy days I crave mung bean pancakes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 녹두를 갈아서 부친 전으로, 대표적인 녹두 요리예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pancake made from ground mung beans, the classic mung bean dish.

phrases.example: 몸이 안 좋을 때 녹두죽을 먹어요.
phrases.en: I eat mung bean porridge when I'm unwell.
phrases.nuance_ko: 녹두로 쑨 죽이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A porridge made from mung beans.

phrases.example: 녹두 한 봉지로 죽을 두 번 끓였어요.
phrases.en: I made porridge twice from one bag of mung beans.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재료를 세는 말과 함께 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase that pairs the ingredient with a counting word.

explain_en: In Korean food it often forms dish names like '녹두전' (mung bean pancake) and '녹두죽'. Bean sprouts (숙주나물) are also grown from mung beans, so they are good to learn together. Hulled mung beans are yellow.

examples.en: I put oyster mushrooms in the soybean paste stew.
Oyster mushrooms are tasty if you tear them and stir-fry them.
I bought a bag of oyster mushrooms at the mart.
The oyster mushrooms are fresh, so the aroma is good.
Add oyster mushrooms and tofu to the hot pot.
I often eat stir-fried oyster mushrooms as a side dish.

explain: 한국 요리에서 자주 쓰는 버섯이고 찌개, 전골, 볶음에 많이 들어가요. 표고버섯보다 부드럽고 향이 약해요. 그냥 '느타리'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I bought oyster mushrooms at the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: '느타리버섯'을 줄여서 편하게 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual short form of 느타리버섯.

phrases.en: I made stir-fried oyster mushrooms as a side dish.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한국 밥상에 자주 나오는 반찬 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A side dish name that often appears on Korean tables.

phrases.en: I tear the oyster mushrooms by hand and add them.
phrases.nuance_ko: 칼보다 손으로 찢어서 요리하는 방법을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the way of tearing them by hand instead of cutting.

explain_en: This mushroom is common in Korean cooking and goes into stews, hot pots and stir-fries. It is softer and milder in aroma than shiitake ('표고버섯'). People also say just '느타리'.

examples.en: My friend is a well-known big eater.

examples.ko: 대식가인 형 때문에 냉장고가 금방 비어요.
examples.en: The fridge empties quickly because of my big-eating brother.
I'm a big eater, so at a buffet I get my money's worth.

examples.ko: 우리 가족은 모두 대식가여서 쌀이 빨리 떨어져요.
examples.en: Our whole family eats a lot, so we run out of rice quickly.

examples.ko: 그렇게 작은 몸으로 대식가라니 믿기지 않아요.
examples.en: I can't believe such a small person is a big eater.
This restaurant is really great for big eaters.

explain: 많이 먹는 사람을 말하고, 칭찬이나 놀림 둘 다 가볍게 쓸 수 있어요. 아이나 친구끼리는 '먹보'라고도 해요. 반대로 적게 먹는 사람은 '소식가'라고 불러요.

phrases.example: 저는 대식가라서 밥을 세 그릇 먹어요.
phrases.en: I'm a big eater, so I eat three bowls of rice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기나 다른 사람을 소개할 때 쓰는 존댓말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite form for describing yourself or others.

phrases.example: 우리 동생은 먹보라서 간식을 다 먹어요.
phrases.en: My little brother is a glutton, so he eats all the snacks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구나 아이끼리 가볍게 놀릴 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A playful teasing word among friends or kids.

phrases.en: I eat little, so I get full easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대식가'의 반대말로, 적게 먹는 사람이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 대식가: someone who eats little.

explain_en: It refers to someone who eats a lot and can be used lightly as either a compliment or a tease. Among kids and friends people also say '먹보'. The opposite, a light eater, is '소식가'.

examples.en: I had stone pot bibimbap for lunch.
If you cook rice in a stone pot, scorched rice forms at the bottom.
The stone pot is very hot, so be careful.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 돌솥으로 밥을 지어 줘요.
examples.en: This restaurant cooks the rice in a stone pot.

examples.ko: 돌솥이 나올 때 지글지글 소리가 났어요.
examples.en: A sizzling sound came from the stone pot when it was brought out.

examples.ko: 돌솥에서 막 나온 밥이 정말 맛있어요.
examples.en: Rice fresh out of the stone pot is really delicious.

explain: 음식 이름 앞에 붙어 '돌솥비빔밥', '돌솥밥'처럼 많이 나와요. 열을 오래 간직해서 음식이 끝까지 따뜻하고, 밥이 눌어 누룽지가 생겨요. 흙으로 만든 '뚝배기'와 비슷하게 뜨거운 채로 나오니 조심해야 해요.

phrases.en: I ordered stone-pot rice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돌솥에 지은 밥 요리를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: A dish of rice cooked in a stone pot.

phrases.en: The stone pot is hot, so be careful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당에서 주의를 줄 때 자주 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often heard as a warning in restaurants.

phrases.en: I scraped up and ate the crispy rice from the stone pot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돌솥 바닥에 눌은 밥을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The scorched rice at the bottom of the pot.

explain_en: It often appears in food names such as '돌솥비빔밥' and '돌솥밥'. It holds heat for a long time, so the food stays hot and the rice gets scorched at the bottom. Like an earthenware '뚝배기', it comes out very hot, so be careful.

examples.en: If you grind perilla seeds and put them in soup, it tastes nutty.

examples.ko: 엄마가 시장에서 들깨 한 봉지를 사 오셨어요.
examples.en: Mom bought a bag of perilla seeds at the market.
I want to eat perilla noodle soup.
We planted perilla in the field and it is growing well.
If you press oil from perilla seeds, it becomes perilla oil.

examples.ko: 들깨 향이 강해서 저는 조금만 넣어요.
examples.en: The perilla smell is strong, so I add only a little.

explain: '들깨'는 참깨와 다른 식물이에요. 씨를 갈아 국이나 나물에 넣고, 기름은 '들기름', 잎은 '깻잎'이라고 불러요.

phrases.example: 국에 들깨 가루를 한 숟가락 넣었어요.
phrases.en: I put a spoonful of ground perilla seeds in the soup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들깨를 갈아 만든 가루로, 국이나 나물에 넣어 고소하게 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Ground perilla seeds, added to soups or seasoned greens for a nutty flavor.

phrases.example: 비 오는 날에는 들깨 칼국수가 생각나요.
phrases.en: On rainy days I crave perilla seed kalguksu.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들깨로 국물을 낸 칼국수 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name of kalguksu made with a perilla seed broth.

phrases.en: I seasoned the greens with perilla oil.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들깨로 짠 기름이에요. 참기름과 맛이 달라요.
phrases.nuance_en: Oil pressed from perilla seeds; it tastes different from sesame oil.

explain_en: '들깨' is a different plant from sesame (참깨). The seeds are ground into soups or side dishes, the oil is called '들기름', and the leaves are called '깻잎'.

examples.ko: 이 커피는 시럽을 너무 많이 넣어서 들척지근해요.
examples.en: This coffee has too much syrup, so it's sickly sweet.
If I drink sugary drinks, my mouth feels sticky.
I like that the pumpkin porridge isn't as cloyingly sweet as I expected.

examples.ko: 입안이 들척지근해서 물을 한 잔 마셨어요.
examples.en: My mouth tasted sickly sweet, so I drank a glass of water.

examples.ko: 이 빵은 들척지근하기만 하고 맛은 별로예요.
examples.en: This bread is just cloyingly sweet and doesn't taste good.

examples.ko: 과일 주스가 너무 들척지근하면 물을 타 마셔요.
examples.en: If fruit juice is too sweet, I add water and drink it.

explain: '달콤하다'는 기분 좋은 단맛인데, '들척지근하다'는 너무 달아서 느끼하고 물릴 때 써요. 부담 없이 적당히 단 맛은 '달짝지근하다'라고 해요. 입안이 끈적할 만큼 단 음료나 빵에 자주 어울려요.

phrases.en: This drink has a cloyingly sweet taste.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ'으로 맛을 꾸밀 때 쓰고, 너무 달아서 물린다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-ㄴ' form describes a taste, with the sense of being sickly sweet.

phrases.example: 이 빵은 너무 달아서 많이 못 먹겠어요.
phrases.en: This bread is too sweet, so I can't eat much.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 쉽고 평범한 말로, 맛이 너무 달다고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler, plainer way to say something is too sweet.

phrases.en: I like this juice because it isn't sickly sweet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정 표현을 써서 너무 달지 않아 좋다는 뜻을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says it is not overly sweet, which is a good thing.

explain_en: '달콤하다' is a pleasant sweetness, while '들척지근하다' is for something so sweet it feels cloying and makes you tired of it. A mildly, comfortably sweet taste is '달짝지근하다'. It suits drinks or bread so sweet that your mouth feels sticky.

examples.en: The hot broth warms my body.
The floor is nicely warm, so it is good for lying down.
They just took out fresh warm bread at the bakery.
On cold days I drink tea hot.
The hand warmer is nice and warm.
If the bath water is nicely hot, your tiredness goes away.

explain: '뜨겁다'는 데일 만큼 뜨거울 때도 쓰지만, '따끈하다'는 기분 좋게 따뜻한 정도예요. 국, 빵, 방바닥, 목욕물처럼 먹거나 몸에 닿는 것에 많이 써요. '따뜻하다'보다 조금 더 열이 있는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I bought warm bread this morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 막 구운 것처럼 기분 좋게 따뜻한 음식에 '따끈한'을 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '따끈한' describes food that is pleasantly warm, as if freshly made.

phrases.en: It is nice and toasty under the blanket.
phrases.nuance_ko: '따끈하다'를 반복해서 더 포근하고 귀여운 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: The repeated form sounds cozier and cuter than 따끈하다.

phrases.en: The soup has cooled down, so it is not warm anymore.
phrases.nuance_ko: '따끈하다'의 부정형으로, 음식이 식었을 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, often used when food has cooled.

explain_en: 뜨겁다 can mean hot enough to burn, but 따끈하다 is pleasantly hot. It is used for things you eat or touch, like soup, bread, a heated floor or a bath. It feels a little hotter than 따뜻하다.
